ideas: Cheap goods and online shopping encourage overbuying
Environmental cost of fast fashion and waste
Growing interest in minimalism among young people

phrases.meaning: a society focused on buying things
cheap clothes made quickly and thrown away

phrases.phrase: at the click of a button
keep up with the latest trends

model: Yes, I think most people in cities own far more than they need. The main reason is that shopping has become too easy. You can buy almost anything at the click of a button, and apps like Shopee send daily discounts that make people feel they're missing out. Fast fashion is the clearest example. Many people buy clothes just to keep up with the latest trends, wear them twice, and then throw them away, so a huge amount ends up in landfill. We've basically become a throwaway society. I noticed this last year, when I moved flats. I found a whole bag of clothes that I'd never worn, and I felt a bit embarrassed. After that, I decided to declutter, and I gave most of it to a charity. To be fair, owning more things is partly a sign of a higher standard of living, and people in Vietnam have far more than their parents did, which is a good thing. But I'd say consumer culture has gone too far, and buying less would make most of us happier.
